rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction and no-fault relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Once you have lived in your unit lawfully for 12 months, your landlord can end your tenancy only for a just cause listed in the law, and the written notice must state that cause. For a no-fault cause such as owner move-in, taking the unit off the market, or demolition or major remodel, the landlord must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance within 15 days or waive your last month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of tenancy; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property in California, including mobilehome park units, once the tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the unit for 12 months. If an adult tenant is added before 24 months, it applies only when all tenants have occupied 12+ months or at least one has occupied 24+ months. Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years is not covered (except mobilehomes). Does not apply where a qualifying local just cause ordinance (such as the Los Angeles JCO or RSO) covers the unit.
rules.exemptions: Transient or tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and residential care facilities; school dormitories; units where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with an owner who lives there; owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms (including ADUs and JADUs); owner-occupied duplexes where the owner lived in one unit at the start of the tenancy (neither unit an ADU or JADU); housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the last 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable units (such as single-family homes or condos) not owned by a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, if the tenant got the required written exemption notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; mobilehome homeowners.
rules.penalty: A noncompliant termination notice is void. An owner who tries to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, attorney's fees and costs at the court's discretion, and up to three times actual damages plus punitive damages for willful conduct, oppression, fraud or malice. The Attorney General and the city attorney or county counsel may seek an injunction.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied duplex: owner lived in one of two units in a single structure at the start of the tenancy and still lives there; neither unit is an ADU or JADU
Separately alienable unit (single-family home or condo) whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, where the tenant received the statutory exemption notice
Owner-occupied single-family residence where the owner rents no more than two units or bedrooms, including an ADU or JADU

rules.conflict_note: Under subdivision (i), the section does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 covers the unit, or where a later local ordinance is more protective and the city has made a binding finding; less protective local ordinances adopted after that date are unenforceable. This is ordinary precedence. The section was re-enacted with an operative date of April 1, 2024, amended by AB 1529 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 203) effective January 1, 2026, and sunsets January 1, 2030; the just-cause requirement first took effect January 1, 2020.
rules.reason: Both candidates describe the same Tenant Protection Act just-cause section (Civ. Code § 1946.2), so they were merged; the 15-year age test was kept as coverage, the tenancy-length condition was removed from building coverage, and untestable exemptions were moved to text.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act relocation for lower-income households displaced by demolition
rules.requirement: If your protected unit is demolished for new housing and your household earns 80% of area median income or less, you must receive relocation benefits equal to those public entities pay under Gov. Code § 7260 et seq. In Los Angeles, the owner pays the HCA amount or the city amount, whichever is higher.
rules.key_value: Relocation consistent with Gov. Code § 7260 et seq. for lower-income households
rules.coverage_conditions: Protected units demolished for new housing development; applies to lower-income occupants (80% AMI or below).

unresolvable_conditions: Unit must be a protected unit being demolished for a new housing development
Occupant household must be lower income (80% AMI or below)

rules.reason: Single candidate on the Housing Crisis Act relocation requirement, a separate statute from the other candidates.

rules.title: Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement displacement under 20 days (San Francisco)
rules.requirement: If you must move out for less than 20 days for capital improvement work in San Francisco, your relocation payment is set by Civil Code § 1947.9 rather than the city's Rent Ordinance § 37.9C. For notices served March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027, that is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses.
rules.key_value: $446.00/day per household plus actual moving expenses (notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in San Francisco rent-controlled units temporarily displaced for less than 20 days for capital improvement work.

unresolvable_conditions: Unit must be in San Francisco and subject to the San Francisco Rent Ordinance

rules.conflict_note: The state statute, not S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C, sets relocation for temporary capital improvement displacements under 20 days; this is settled precedence, not an open conflict. The March 1, 2026 date is an annual rate adjustment, not the statute's effective date.
rules.reason: Both candidates are San Francisco Rent Board statements that Civ. Code § 1947.9 governs relocation for sub-20-day capital improvement displacements, so they were merged.
